item.title: China Stock Premium Over Hong Kong Widens on State Intervention
item.description: Beijing’s efforts to stabilize its equity markets are helping drive the pricing gap between dual-listed stocks in China and Hong Kong to the widest level in nearly 17 months.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Yang

item.title: Gold Holds Above $4,000 as Traders Look to Fed Rate Decision
item.description: Gold steadied above $4,000 an ounce as dip buyers entered the market before the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision due later Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Dongshan Precision Set to Debut After $1.3 Billion HK Listing
item.description: Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co. is set to begin trading in Hong Kong on Wednesday after raising HK$9.9 billion ($1.3 billion), a debut that will test appetite for artificial intelligence-linked listings after a sharp market pullback.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Haiti Crisis: El Salvador Surges Hundreds of Troops to Find Missing Soldiers
item.description: El Salvador’s troop presence in Haiti has swelled to at least 600, according to a top researcher, a reflection of President Nayib Bukele’s efforts to find four kidnapped soldiers in the troubled Caribbean nation.
item.dc:creator: Jim Wyss

item.title: Stocks in Asia Advance on Resurgent AI Optimism: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks rose, tracking gains on Wall Street as renewed enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence trade lifted equities ahead of earnings from tech megacaps and the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder and Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 28
item.description: Oil held a two-day drop as traders tracked a tight Israeli election that’ll help to shape the course of the US war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Lorelei Smillie

item.title: Dallas Mavericks CEO on Team Investment and New Stadium
item.description: Dallas Mavericks CEO Rick Welts discusses the long-term capital required to build and sustain a professional sports enterprise with Bloomberg’s Randall Williams at Bloomberg Invest Dallas 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Prediction Market Betting Stretches Past Sports
item.description: The rapid growth of prediction markets is raising questions about sports wagering, younger traders, market manipulation, and regulation. Sean Patrick Maloney, CEO and President of the Coalition for Prediction Markets, argues federally regulated platforms should be treated as financial markets overseen by a well-funded CFTC, rather than casinos. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the industry's safeguards, the controversy surrounding sports contracts, and why he expects prediction markets to expand further into politics and financial markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wells Fargo, UBS & Citi on Servicing the Texas Wealthy
item.description: Wells Fargo Head of Central Division Wealth & Investment Management Heather Hunt-Ruddy; UBS Managing Director of Global Family & Institutional Wealth William Thompson and Citi Managing Director & Central Region Market Executive Clinton Warren discuss how wealth managers are serving affluent clients relocating to North Texas with Bloomberg’s Sarah McGregor at Bloomberg Invest Dallas 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nasdaq Texas & Walmart Discuss Corp Listing Strategies
item.description: Nasdaq Texas President Rachel Racz and Walmart Senior Vice President & Head of Investor Relations Stephanie Wissink discuss how exchanges and public companies are navigating listings, investor engagement and long-term shareholder value with Bloomberg's Amanda Cantrell at Bloomberg Invest Dallas 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPM's Agather & Herbst on Texas Wealth Wave
item.description: J.P. Morgan Private Bank Global Vice Chair and JPMorgan Chase Dallas Region Chairman, Elaine Agather and J.P. Morgan Private Bank Managing Director & Head of Dallas, Ashley Herbst discuss capital inflows, generational wealth transfer and Texas’ changing investment landscape with Bloomberg’s Joe Lovinger at Bloomberg Invest Dallas 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Montage Intl. CEO: Future Bookings Are Higher Into 2027
item.description: Alan Fuerstman, Founder and CEO of Montage International, said luxury travel demand has remained resilient despite higher costs and geopolitical uncertainty. He described the business as coming off a record year and said future bookings are up going into next year, with record holiday-period bookings at resorts across the U.S. and Mexico. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia’s MSCI Downgrade Threat – What It Means for Investors: Podcast
item.description: MSCI’s double downgrade warning sparked Indonesia's sharpest market selloff in nearly 30 years. Now, billions in foreign capital are on the line.
item.dc:creator: K Oanh Ha and Naomi Ng

item.title: Catastrophe, Rogue AI and Other Anthropic IPO Risks
item.description: Anthropic is headed for what could be history’s biggest IPO, warning that its product could be catastrophic for humanity. On the Big Take podcast, what the share offering means for AI, markets and everyone else. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Raizen Debt to Be Eyed by FS, Mubadala in Restructuring
item.description: Brazilian biofuel producer FS — Fueling Sustainability and Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Co. are seeking to buy debt held by creditors of troubled biofuel giant Raizen SA, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Gamarski, Cristiane Lucchesi and Dayanne Sousa

item.title: Barclays Sees FX Volatility Staying Elevated as Dollar Rises
item.description: Barclays Plc strategists expect volatility in Group-of-10 currencies to rise and remain elevated as the dollar strengthens and interest-rate swings increase.
item.dc:creator: Melos Ambaye

item.title: Real Estate Investors on Commercial Market Opportunities
item.description: Hines Co-CEO, Laura Hines-Pierce; Crow Holdings Chief Investment Officer, Michael Hyun and JLL Senior Managing Director and North Texas Broker Lead, Torrey Littlejohn discuss valuations, capital deployment and the next commercial real estate investment cycle with Bloomberg’s Joe Lovinger at Bloomberg Invest Dallas 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sports Leagues Evolving Rules For Investment: Charles
item.description: Ian Charles, managing partner & CEO of Arctos and partner & head of KKR Solutions at KKR, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." They discuss the challenges of investing in sports franchises and the build of 'hoard' of zombie funds and firms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Eliud Kipchoge Takes His Running Mission Worldwide
item.description: Eliud Kipchoge is taking the next chapter of his legendary marathon career around the world. The two-time Olympic marathon champion, who became the first person to run a marathon in under two hours, is embarking on a multi-year World Tour that will take him across all seven continents. Fresh off a victory and course record at the Melbourne Marathon, Kipchoge joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss his mission to inspire more people to run, the mental challenge of breaking the two-hour barrier, and the philosophy behind his mantra “No Human Is Limited.” He also discusses his decades-long partnership with Nike to help transform racing-shoe technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banks Eye $21 Billion Bonds for Broadcom Chip-Financing Deal
item.description: Banks are planning to sell as much as about $21 billion of high-grade bonds as soon as early next year as part of a $63 billion funding package that Broadcom Inc. has pulled together to help finance chips for AI developer Anthropic PBC.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia
